newsitem.title: USA: COMEnergy sees Mass. power unit back Oct 1.
newsitem.headline: COMEnergy sees Mass. power unit back Oct 1.

text.p: Commonwealth Energy Co expected its 584 megawatt (MW) Canal Generating Station unit 2 would resume full commercial operation October 1, the company said Thursday.
The unit has been in an overhaul for more than a year so it could use natural gas in addition to one-percent sulphur number six fuel oil to generate electricity, company spokesman James Rappoli said.
The utility decided to upgrade the plant to give it more flexibility and because gas is cleaner burning than oil, he said.
Rappoli said the unit has been generating power to the New England Power Pool at 500-530 MW as it was undergoing startup testing with oil.
"The unit will be testing on gas next week," he said.
When the overhaul is completed, Canal unit 2 could burn up to 75,000 million British thermal units per day of natural gas or 10,000 barrels per day of fuel oil, Rappoli said.
Commonwealth Energy's Canal Electric Co subsidiary is the operator of the plant, and jointly owns the unit with Montaup Electric Co, a subsidiary of Eastern Utilities Associates.
Canal Electric also operates and wholly-owns the adjoining 560 MW unit 1.
The Canal Generating Station is located in Sandwich, Mass.
